newsitem.title: UK: Ending a mid-summer fling, coffee prices tumble.
newsitem.headline: Ending a mid-summer fling, coffee prices tumble.

text.p: Coffee prices have tumbled after flirting with their firmest values in almost a year, on a view that U.S. supply isn't as tight as it had seemed.

Speculative and commission house selling pressured Arabica type coffree futures on the New York Coffee Sugar and Cocoa Exchange for a second straight day on Wednesday, with the December contract down at 118.25 cents per pound by midday.
Coffee futures fell after a rise in U.S. warehouse stocks was reported. Late on Monday the exchange said stockpiles rose by 4,797 (132-pound/ 60-kilo) bags in the week to August 23.

London Robusta coffee futures again found themselves tracking the New York lead. The most-traded November contract closed $57 per tonne down at $1,633 a tonne, hovering just around critical technical support.

Analysts predicted that this might hold, also noting that cool weather in Brazil. But technical analyst Elli Gifford of Investment Research said the slide hinted that the market could have seen the best of its rally for the time being.
Elsewhere in the commodity sector, oil prices rallied again with the help of news of a draw in U.S. stocks of refined oil products after surrendering on Tuesday some recent sharp gains.
London October futures for North Sea benchmark Brent Blend crude oil at 1645 GMT were up by almost 40 cents a barrel at around $20.40.
American Petroleum Institute statistics for the week to August 23 showed gasoline stocks down 2.238 million barrels.

Most other commodities traded in narrow ranges with gold ending in London unchanged from Tuesday at $388.55 per ounce and the flagship industrial metal, copper, trapped in a band on the London Metal Exchange. It barely reacted to news that workers at Chile state producer Codelco's Salvador mine voted to strike from Saturday to demand wage rises. Output at this mine is only a modest 85,000 tonnes a year. Last afternoon business was at $1,943 a tonne, down just $1 from Tuesday. Chicago Board of Trade (CBOT) wheat futures eased slightly but held in a range just either side of $4.55 per bushel.
